note: bare-shape classes (rect class=group/store/node, not <g>-wrapped) -> CLASS_PLACEMENT
bare-shape classes (rect/text class=node/group/store, not <g>-wrapped) -> CLASS_PLACEMENT; also fill="none" attrs -> PAINT_ATTR

embedded <style> block + hex color literals -> STYLE_BLOCK + COLOR_LITERAL; four of the warnings are pre-existing TEXT_OVERFLOW near the right margin, and three are COLOUR_NO_GLYPH on its "node blue" boxes. Its fourth blue box escapes only because its label reads "first 3 + [+N more]": the rule demands the treatment's OWN glyph, and blue's is "+", a character prose uses too. That residual is recorded rather than fixed — see the KNOWN LIMITATION note on COLOUR_NO_GLYPH — because the alternative is taking "+" away from blue, and "+" is the diff convention every reader already knows. This fixture is the pin for it

embedded <style> block with CSS custom properties -> STYLE_BLOCK. The one warning is a TEXT_OVERFLOW on its <text class="groupLabel"> at line 50, and it appeared when the group/region style test moved from a SUBSTRING check over the ancestor-class string to token membership: "groupLabel" used to match "group" by substring and so was modeled 12px start-anchored, which is not what the CSS does — `.group` selects the class token, never a prefix of a longer name. Dropping that accidental match is correct; what the estimator then falls back to is the class-less guess `middle`, and the warning is the width of THAT guess, not a measurement of how the element really renders. It is accepted rather than fixed because the only thing that anchors this element is the fixture's own inline <style> block, which the linter refuses to read by design — refusing it is this fixture's primary expectation. So: an accepted warning on an element whose real styling is deliberately out of reach, and the pin for the token semantics
<script>/<foreignObject>/<image> present -> BANNED_ELEMENT (ban-list line 155)

<g class="node red purple"> -> exactly one TREATMENT_COMBO failure, the mirror of SHAPE_COMBO one level up: a box makes ONE claim about itself and the stylesheet can only paint one of the two. Its label states both glyphs, so the failure is isolated from COLOUR_NO_GLYPH. The "node grey dim" beside it is the legal stacking (see pass-treatments.svg, where a PASS verdict proves it)
<g class="node store"> -> exactly one SHAPE_COMBO failure; the retired legacy combo
<rect class="proc"> -> CLASS_PLACEMENT; the 17 silhouettes belong on a <g>
a table nested inside an llm -> one NEST_PARENT failure and nothing else; an llm may not hold anything, so it is never also told to add "holds"
a proc nested inside a table -> NEST_PARENT; a table's interior is its own body cells, and a cell is the one child any silhouette may take
a proc nested inside a lane -> NEST_PARENT; a lane is a swimlane HEADER, a small box with a lifeline dropping below it, and the contract names it never-a-parent twice and gives it no content-well row
machine > store > table -> NEST_DEPTH; the limit is two levels of component nesting

four SHAPE_TEXT_FIT warnings, never a failure: an fn label wider than W-40, and — since the rule measures path-drawn silhouettes too — a store wider than W-40, a decision wider than W-60 and a cloud wider than W-60

left: an fn rect overhanging a pkg well on both sides -> NEST_WELL. middle: a proc holding a component without "holds" -> HOLDS_MISSING, and the parent is nestable so the advice is actionable. right: a type overhanging node's own well -> NEST_WELL. All warn-tier

two NEST_WELL warnings through a bare <g>: the first pkg wraps its own body rect, the second fn wraps its child rect. Geometry is collected through any <g> that names no silhouette, so a wrapper cannot switch NEST_WELL and SHAPE_TEXT_FIT off while every number still parses and nothing reports it

"holds" on a childless proc and on a childless unclassed <g> -> two HOLDS_EMPTY. The modifier restyles the label to a muted 12px band by class alone, so a <g> that names no silhouette gets the same silent visual regression

width="180px" (legal SVG), width="abc" (a typo) and font-size="NaN" (which parses as a float, then compares False against everything) -> three GEOM_UNPARSEABLE warnings; without the rule all three boxes report clean while the checks that read those numbers are switched off or silently defaulted

a proc and a store nested inside a "node holds" -> clean; node is a plain rounded rect with a real interior and its own content well, so the fallback silhouette is no less capable than the silhouettes it stands in for

two swimlane headers with lifelines dropping below them and each participant's boxes drawn as SIBLINGS on its lifeline -> clean; this is the markup a sequence diagram uses, and the shape a lane may never take is in fail-nest-parent-lane.svg

three boxes no rule may guess at -> clean: a node drawing only sparkle paths and no body rect (a rect-drawn silhouette without its rect is not measured), a child carrying <path d="Z"> with no moveto (which must contribute no point rather than the origin), and a group smaller than its own well insets (an inverted well is skipped, not reported against every child)
a cell stack inside a type and inside a queue -> clean; Q11 makes a type's fields and a queue's items cells, and a cell is data rather than a component, so it is legal inside any silhouette

an iface and a machine whose labels fill their contract width exactly -> no SHAPE_TEXT_FIT; pins that the width table is measured against the box W, not the narrower body rect those two draw (subtracting both would warn on a correctly sized box)

clean contract-conforming fragment from this spec's own doc, renamed to the treatments (warn->yellow, danger->red) and given each treatment's glyph in its label — a shipped worked example has to follow the rule it demonstrates, and COLOUR_NO_GLYPH is covered properly by the dedicated warn-colour-* fixtures. Its "edge red" arrows carry no glyph and never needed one: an edge has no label of its own

contract-conforming fragment from this spec's own doc; its two former "node store" boxes are now "file" documents, and its two "node blue" boxes now lead their labels with the + they were marking in colour alone. The one remaining warning is the pre-existing TEXT_OVERFLOW on an edgeLabel near the right margin — unrelated to the shape kit and older than this job, which is why this entry is 1 rather than 0

all 17 new silhouettes, each correctly classed on its own <g>, plus spark on <path>. The cloud is the contract's own recipe, whose three arc endpoints walk x from X to X+W, so its measured width is exactly W and its W-60 row is really checked

the five legal containments (store>table, machine>proc+store, pkg>fn, proc>iface, ui>cell), every parent carrying "holds" and every child — including the iface lollipop knob, which is a <circle> outside its rect — inside the parent's well. Its "cell green" now reads "✓ working" rather than leaving the tick to the paint

combos that must NOT trip SHAPE_COMBO: cell head, node blue, bar green, region yellow, store holds, edge dashed green, a spark path inside an agent, and ui > table > cell. Both "holds" parents really do hold something, so neither draws HOLDS_EMPTY. The one warning is COLOUR_NO_GLYPH on its "node blue", a true positive; the treated bar, region and edge beside it stay silent, which is what pins their exemptions

all six treatments on boxes — grey, red, yellow, green, blue, purple — each stating its OWN glyph, so the pairing COLOUR_NO_GLYPH demands is pinned by a fixture that emits nothing at all. The seventh box is "node grey dim": the one legal stacking in the palette, and the only place a PASS verdict proves TREATMENT_COMBO does not count "dim" (a fail fixture could not — the manifest pins the failure VERDICT, never the failure count, so an extra failure there would be invisible)

<path class="edge blue"> and <path class="edge grey"> -> clean; a treatment is legal on an edge as well as on a box, and an edge is never asked for a glyph of its own (its mark, when it has one, rides on the edgeLabel beside it)

two COLOUR_NO_GLYPH, one per way of failing the rule: a "node yellow" whose label says nothing about why it is yellow, and a "node purple" labelled "✓ shipped" — the WRONG treatment's glyph, which the rule counts as no glyph at all because a mark contradicting the paint is worse in greyscale than a bare box. Everything beside them is a control that must stay quiet: a "node green" stating ✓, a "node red" covered by an adjacent "pill red" stating ✗, an unlabelled "bar purple", a "region grey", and an "edge blue" path

four glyphless "node red" boxes and ONE "pill red" legend -> three COLOUR_NO_GLYPH, not zero. The adjacent-pill escape is a budget: a pill answers for one box and is then spent. As a predicate it was defeated by exactly the pattern it was written to catch — hermes fragments are flat, so every part is a sibling of every other, and one pill in a corner silenced the whole figure. The "node green" states its own glyph and never touches the budget

three tables, two COLOUR_AS_CATEGORY. (1) five flat cells in three treatments with no header cell -> hue is doing a category's job. (2) the same colouring row-grouped, with the "cell head" in a <g> row of its own and the data cells in another: MUST NOT fire, and did fire before the rule grouped cells by their table instead of by their immediate parent — the cry-wolf case, on completely ordinary markup. (3) the same rainbow split across two row <g>s with no header anywhere: MUST fire, and was silent for the mirror-image reason. Every cell states its glyph, so the count isolates this rule from COLOUR_NO_GLYPH

two fn boxes each carrying a repo-relative data-code, and the edge between them carrying one too -> clean, and clean WITH --code-refs on, which is the only entry in this manifest that sets "code_refs". Every path holds a "/", so CODE_REF_BASENAME stays quiet; the "pill" beside them deliberately carries no ref at all and must stay quiet under the flag, which is what pins the parts exemption (a terminal tag stands for no code, so there is nothing it could honestly link to). All three refs name real locations in this repo — a fixture for a rule about refs being verifiable claims cannot itself cite invented ones

data-code="internal/api/board.go#37" -> exactly one CODE_REF_FORMAT failure. The hash is the mistake the convention exists to prevent: the separator is a colon, and a hash followed by 3-8 hex digits would ALSO fail the fragment as a COLOR_LITERAL, with a message about paint. This one's "37" is two digits, so it stays under that scan and the failure is isolated to the rule under test
